eligible_items.display_summary: DHS wants to raise the cost of applying for US citizenship (Form N-400) from $760 to $1,330 on paper, and $710 to $1,280 online, with the appeal of a denial (Form N-336) going from $830 to $1,475. Reduced fees and fee waivers for naturalisation would end. Anyone can comment for 60 days once the proposed rule is published.
eligible_items.display_summary_es: El gobierno propone subir el costo de solicitar la ciudadanía (Form N-400) de $760 a $1,330 en papel y de $710 a $1,280 en línea, subir a $1,475 la apelación de una negativa (Form N-336), y eliminar las tarifas reducidas y las exenciones de pago (fee waivers) para estos trámites. Cualquier persona podrá enviar comentarios durante los 60 días siguientes a la publicación oficial de la propuesta en el Federal Register, fecha que aún no se confirma.
eligible_items.key_date_raw: Submission of Public Comments: Written comments must be submitted on or before August 24, 2026. The electronic Federal Docket Management System will accept comments prior to midnight ET at the end of that day.

eligible_items.what_to_watch_for: DHS's proposed rule would raise the N-400 fee from $760 to $1,330 (paper) and $710 to $1,280 (online), raise N-336 from $830 to $1,475, and eliminate reduced fees and fee waivers for naturalization filings. Watch for the rule's actual Federal Register publication date, which starts the 60-day public comment clock.

eligible_items.display_summary: Adults who want to take custody of an immigrant child who arrived without a parent or guardian would have to show more documents — proof of identity, proof of income, and information for background checks — before the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) releases the child to them. Comments on the proposed rule are open until August 25, 2026.
eligible_items.display_summary_es: Las personas que quieren hacerse cargo de un niño migrante bajo custodia del gobierno (el sponsor o patrocinador) tendrían que presentar documentos específicos de identidad y comprobante de ingresos, además de más datos para la verificación de antecedentes, según una propuesta de la Oficina de Reasentamiento de Refugiados (ORR). Todavía no está en vigor: es un proyecto de reglamento abierto a comentarios del público hasta el 25 de agosto de 2026.
eligible_items.key_date_raw: Consideration will be given to comments on this rulemaking received on or before August 25, 2026.

eligible_items.display_summary: The comment deadline closes on the DHS rule requiring foreign nationals in the US to register with the government and give fingerprints (Form G-325R). DHS is asking whether more immigration filings should count as registration on their own, and whether to change biometrics rules for some travelers; further rulemaking may follow.
eligible_items.display_summary_es: El Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DHS) recibe comentarios del público sobre posibles cambios al registro obligatorio de inmigrantes (Formulario G-325R), entre ellos ampliar qué solicitudes de inmigración ya cuentan como registro y modificar la toma de datos biométricos a ciertos viajeros. Cualquier persona puede comentar hasta que cierre el expediente, y DHS podría emitir después una nueva regla basada en lo que reciba.

eligible_items.what_to_watch_for: DHS is taking public comment on possible future changes to the registration framework, including expanding the list of immigration filings that automatically satisfy registration and modifying biometric procedures for certain travelers. Watch for the docket closing and any follow-on rulemaking DHS issues based on the comments.

eligible_items.display_summary: DHS is expected to publish a proposed rule on getting a green card by investing in a US business (EB-5). It would change how Regional Centers — entities approved to pool investor money into projects — are designated and terminated, how long money must stay invested, USCIS audit powers, protections for good-faith investors, and automatic revocation of petitions.
eligible_items.display_summary_es: El DHS tiene pendiente publicar en el Federal Register una propuesta de reglamento (RIN 1615-AC94) para las personas que obtienen la green card invirtiendo en un negocio en Estados Unidos (EB-5), con cambios en cómo se aprueba o se termina a un Regional Center —la entidad que agrupa el dinero de los inversionistas— y en la revocación automática de peticiones, entre otros puntos. Al publicarse abre un período en el que cualquier persona puede enviar comentarios.
eligible_items.key_date_raw: Submission of Public Comments: Written comments must be submitted on or before August 31, 2026. The electronic Federal Docket Management System will accept comments prior to midnight eastern time at the end of that day.

eligible_items.what_to_watch_for: Watch for the Federal Register publication of the NPRM "EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022; Ensuring the Integrity of the EB-5 Program; Automatic Revocation of Petitions for Immigrant Classification," which would amend 8 C.F.R. Parts 204, 205, 216, and 235. Review the regulatory text on Regional Center designation/termination, Forms I-956, I-526E and I-829, investment sustainment, USCIS audit authority, good-faith investor protections, and automatic revocation.

eligible_items.display_summary: Employers using the extra H-2B visas Congress allows for seasonal, non-farm jobs must file a sworn statement (attestation) that they meet the added conditions. The Labor Department is asking the White House budget office (OMB) to renew that collection — the requirement itself is not changing — and comments are open until August 31, 2026.
eligible_items.display_summary_es: El Departamento del Trabajo pide autorización para seguir usando la declaración que los empleadores presentan cuando quieren contratar trabajadores temporales bajo los cupos adicionales de visas H-2B autorizados por el Congreso. No cambia el requisito en sí: es un trámite de renovación, y cualquier persona puede enviar comentarios hasta el 31 de agosto de 2026.
eligible_items.key_date_raw: The OMB will consider all written comments that the agency receives on or before August 31, 2026.

The Department of Labor (DOL) is submitting this Employment and Training Administration (ETA)-sponsored information collection request (ICR) to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review and approval in accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA). Public comments on the ICR are invited.
